title: Customer Journey
description: One blind-testable user journey. The tester receives ONE of these and must fulfil `intent` and verify every `expected_observations` entry — without knowing internal routes, navigating only by visible UI.

id.description: Unique id, e.g. J001. Stable across runs so results can be diffed.

category.description: Capability layer. Recommended generic set: A_anonymous, B_user, C_admin, D_edge. You may add your own (e.g. C_staff, E_superadmin) — keep them domain-neutral.

title.description: Short human title of what is being tested.

actor.description: Fixture archetype key (see config.fixtures) OR the literal "anonymous" for logged-out tests. NOT a raw email — the runner/agent resolves the archetype to credentials from config/env.

starting_url.description: Relative path to begin at (e.g. "/", "/login"). The blind tester may ONLY navigate() to this URL; everything else is reached by clicking visible UI.

intent.description: What the user wants to accomplish, in plain narrative.

expected_observations.description: Observable conditions that must ALL hold for PASS. Phrase them by what a user sees (visible text/role/state), not by internal selectors.

negative.description: If true, the journey expects a failure/blocked state (e.g. wrong password shows an error). PASS = the negative behaviour occurred.

probe_path.description: OPTIONAL, headless-runner only. A deep route to jump to for read-only feature capture (the MCP-free runner is allowed to know routes; the blind MCP tester is NOT and ignores this).

skip_if.description: Optional human-readable precondition to skip this journey when unmet (e.g. "feature X disabled").

requires.description: Optional precondition tags (e.g. "completed_transaction", "random_email"). Domain-neutral; the runner notes unmet ones in the report.
